note_tweet.text:
UPPER RIB MODIFICATION aka Rib resectioning

Shrinking the upper chest.

I don't have a Q/A  _yet_ for this so I'm going to post information about the upcoming surgery being developed.

disclaimer: I used a random ravitch procedure image for effect but this will be different and not include a bar.

---

Potential expectations: Up to 2-4 inches of ribcage reduction. This would mostly be in projection, and slightly width.

Rib Involvement: Rib 1 will remain untouched; Rib 2 (R2) is considered a potential addition dependent on cadaver studies and intraoperative conditions, though the default expectation is that it will not be modified. It would go as far down as ribs 5 or 6 depending on your anatomy. 

Pneumothorax Risk: The surgeon's primary concern is pneumothorax, though the surgical plan avoids depths that would induce it; if it occurs, it is treatable in-hospital via chest tubes.

Anesthesia: Double-lumen endotracheal intubation (splitting to one tube per lung) is considered unnecessary for this procedure as lung deflation is not indicated.

Fixation and Hardware: Screws will secure resorbable bridge plates to rib and sternum bones without penetrating the far side; muscle openings or sub-muscular access may be required to bridge the cartilage. No bar will be used, a reabsorbable plate would be used instead

Skin Separation: Skin separation from the sternum is not expected to be problematic and will be reattached if necessary, though the specific extent of induced separation remains unclear.

Structural Integrity: The forces involved are not expected to cause flail chest or plate failure (shear forces were not specifically discussed).

Surgical: Surgeries will be performed in a fully equipped hospital setting for emergency safety and will be highly documented. The procedure will progress from lower ribs upward, alternating between left and right sides. This is a minor point but was asked.

Mediastinum Resilience: The mediastinum is considered resilient enough to handle deviations more extreme than this procedure, citing Dr Wenlin Wang's work as a precedent. I have not interacted with Dr Wenlin personally, but another girl did get a procedure from him and immediately undid it when she came back to the US. YMMV

Heart Compression: Heart compression is not anticipated to be a substantial issue.

Pectus excavatum: The surgery may still be possible with excavatum in some manner, but a serious case may disqualify for potential heart risks.

Chest Wall Tolerance: The chest wall can withstand significant intervention (citing Wenlin's correction of a childhood surgery adding +4" bilaterally with metal plates).

Relaxin: Relaxing was a big topic for pelvic widening, so I'm just mentioning that Relaxin is not utilized in the concept of this surgery.

Breast implants: Existing breast implants will be removed to allow inframammary fold access and reinserted; fresh implants will be on standby for replacement if deemed necessary.

Surgical Team: A thoracic surgeon and a second plastic surgeon will attend the cadaver study and surgery; Rogers notes familiarity with precarious chest wall reconstructions from non-elective contexts.

Timing Between Surgeries: Rogers advises a wait time of greater than 8 weeks between lower rib surgery and the upper rib attempt.

Lower Ribs: Prior completion of lower ribs is expected to make the subsequent procedure easier or better.

Clavicle Sequencing: Clavicle surgery could precede this procedure without significantly impacting results, though upper chest surgery may mitigate forward shoulder roll resulting from clavicle surgery.

Respiratory Impact: Risks include an estimated 10% loss of vital capacity (max breath volume) and an elevated pneumonia risk for a duration. I had a temporary loss in max breath from my rib 5 and below surgery, and it's definitely unpleasant, but I got used to it after about 3 weeks I'd say.

Post-Op Support: No external bracing or constriction is planned post-surgery; internal screws and plates, along with the intact R1 and likely R2, are deemed sufficient for stability.

Combination Procedures: The surgery will not be combined with other procedures at this time. You should seek lower rib surgery first (ribs 5-12).

Operative Time: Initial surgical time was estimated at 8 hours during an earlier consult, with potential reduction to 4 hours once the procedure becomes routine.
